activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Functions Using Local Linearity and Linearization

feedback.problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{3}{3x-4}$ and $f(2)=\operatorname{ln}⁡2.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=2$ to estimate the value of $f(3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(2)=\operatorname{ln}⁡2,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{3}{3x-4},$ then ${f}^{′}(2)=\frac{3}{3(2)-4}=\frac{3}{2}.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{3}{2}(x-2).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(3)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) & ≈L(3) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{3}{2}(3-2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
